Brian Tse proposes **stronger international cooperation on AI safety, especially between China and the West**, alongside framing their relationship as “cooperative rivalry” or “coopertition”—allowing competition and cooperation to coexist rather than treating countries solely as adversaries. (https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/szwZkDBtW5sECHucy/brian-tse-sino-western-cooperation-in-ai-safety)

The proposed mechanism is to foreground countries’ shared interests in AI security, ethics, and governance, enabling coordination on accidents, misuse, and the race to develop AI instead of allowing competition for technological and military supremacy to dominate. The passage presents this as a direction for reducing risk, rather than specifying an enforceable safeguard against unsafe deployment. (https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/szwZkDBtW5sECHucy/brian-tse-sino-western-cooperation-in-ai-safety)
